name: Whey protein

lead: Whey protein is the liquid fraction of milk left over from cheese making, dried into concentrate, isolate or hydrolysate powders. It is a complete protein that digests quickly and is rich in leucine and other essential amino acids.

Lifters and dieters use it as a convenient way to reach daily protein targets, preserve lean mass while cutting and support muscle gain alongside resistance training. Meta-analyses report a small to moderate benefit for strength and lean mass, larger in older adults and in people who otherwise eat little protein.

paras: Whey supplies a rapid rise in blood amino acids, particularly leucine, which stimulates muscle protein synthesis through mTORC1 signalling. Researchers attribute the benefit mainly to adding to total daily protein, so the advantage over other complete protein sources is reported as small when overall intake is already adequate.

Whey is a food product and legal everywhere. Lactose intolerance or milk allergy can cause digestive symptoms or reactions, and isolates contain less lactose. Quality control varies by brand, with occasional heavy-metal or labelling concerns reported. Studies have found no added benefit from very high intakes, and people with kidney disease are advised to follow medical guidance.
